title: Claude is Modding Two Games On Top of One Another to Create Chaotic Online Videos
key_facts: Videos showing two unrelated games combined, such as Minecraft in Elden Ring or Skate 3 mechanics in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2, have spread on social media over the past week.
GLITCHED says the work is largely attributed to AI-assisted coding with Claude Opus 5.5, using decompiled games.
In many cases the two games run side by side, with the mod passing information between them, rather than being truly merged.
Early examples show broken environments, missing textures and a player trapped in one tested Minecraft-in-Skyrim mod.
Some modders, including ones who use AI themselves, criticize the trend; one said he might stop modding if the scene becomes an AI slop factory.
The projects often rely on code and assets from games their makers do not own, which complicates sharing them.
Most exist as videos, not polished downloads.
quote_evidence: AI-generated game mods have found their latest obsession: taking two completely unrelated games and smashing them together.
In many cases, the two games are effectively running alongside one another, with the mod translating information between them and overlaying elements from one game onto another.
It looks impressive in a 20-second video but actually playing some of these creations is a different story.
why_it_matters_hint: AI coding tools are making game modding much faster, which pleases some fans and worries mod makers.
event_date: Trend over roughly the past week (posts dated 27 Sep to 2 Oct 2026)
